 No. 5 Arizona men’s basketball looks toward home opener against Cal Poly
 Ava Widener , Sports Editor 
 November 5, 2026 
 AIdan Gravelle Arizona men’s basketball player Caleb Holt finishes a layup against San Diego State at McKale Center at ALKEME Arena on Oct. 16. 
 The No. 5 University of Arizona men’s basketball team (0-1) welcomes California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo (1-0) for their home opener on Thursday, Nov. 5 at 8:30 p.m. The Wildcats are looking to bounce back after their 84-75 loss to UCLA in Las Vegas, Nevada . 
 History v Cal Poly  
 This is only the fourth time these two teams have met, with the most recent meeting in the 2018-19 season. The first time they played was during the 1949-50 season where Arizona won 63-53. Each time they have played, it’s been at home for Arizona and they have a 3-0 record.  
 Wildcats to watch  
 In their first game of the season against UCLA, sophomore Ivan Kharchenkov led Arizona with 38 points and 10 rebounds. Kharchenkov is one of two returning starters, with the other being senior Motiejus Krivas.  
 Bryce James made his collegiate debut starting against UCLA after redshirting for Arizona last season. The other two starters were transfer sophomore Derek Dixon and freshman Caleb Holt, who combined for 25 points. 
 Mustangs to watch 
 The Mustangs are coming into this game after taking their first win of the season against California State University San Marcos at home on Monday, Nov. 2, winning 78-62. In their exhibition game against Westmont College, Cal Poly lost 105-93.  
 Junior Hamad Mousa led the way for the Mustangs with 18 points and seven rebounds. Following Mousa, Cayden Ward managed 15 points, 11 rebounds and five assists.  
 Cal Poly’s roster is comprised of 13 returning players from the previous season with two additions. They lost Peter Bandelj, who entered the transfer portal and went to the University of Nevada.
